analysis.title: GS McGeoch - Copper supply and balances underwrite px....GSXGCOPP upsides
key_insights: The desk argues micro supply damage is done and copper balances are tight and tightening. It lists tariff risk, Shanghai CESCO week, and copper miners at a 1-year low relative to the commodity as supports for upside.
Cochilco cut its forecast by 330kt for 2026 and 470kt for 2027, about 800kt in total. The previous update was in August.
Chile production is impaired: September output was -15% y/y and year-to-date output is -9% y/y.
The onshore China copper premium is at record highs. The desk says China is genuinely tight, citing the RMB premium supporting the cash SHFE/LME arbitrage and the SHFE curve.
Chinese inventory (social plus bonded) is -66% y/y and downstream inventory is -8% y/y, which the desk calls too low while the US continues to pull metal.

On LME cancellations to sell against the Chinese premium: the desk estimates all-in cost at about $190/mt, assuming 2 weeks of financing at S+80bps with the LME backwardation. Of 225k MT of on-warrant LME inventory, 147k MT is in New Orleans, which is essentially a COMEX arbitrage option, and it is unclear whether Asian warrants are received immediately.
Mid estimates for bonded/trade-house balances are October BL 260k MT and November BL 180k MT, the latter described as seeming high based on trade house feedback.
The desk says the macro community worries about copper because of AI, rates and energy, which it describes as essentially the same trade. It argues copper cannot collapse with micro this tight.

Copper miners (GSXGCOPP index) are at 1-year lows versus the commodity. The desk says miners are not burdened by debt as in 2016, not overcommitted on projects as in 2013, and not holding post-covid stockpiles as in mid 2020.
The desk expects M&A in miners, and argues that supply chain relocalisation requires more supply while stocks are priced as cheaply as ever.

Key events the desk flags: US midterms (possible tariff friction) and CESCO copper week in Shanghai (Nov 23), where the market will ask about 2027 benchmarks. Chile Q3 weather improved, but accidents could increase the disruption allowance into 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Supply is impaired (Chile -15% y/y in September, Cochilco cuts of 800kt over 2026-27), Chinese inventories are -66% y/y, and miners have clean balance sheets, so the equities at a 1-year low relative to copper look cheap.
tension_points.bear_case: A fresh wave of supply or a major demand contraction, plus macro worries about AI, rates and energy and tariff uncertainty, could keep pressure on copper.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fresh wave of supply or a major demand contraction, such as electrification stalling.
